purpose: First-quarter wave slice for the twelfth Ruleset Card — the §1.3 database-as-a-service card 'The Managed Database' / 'DBaaS' / 'The Cellar' / 'Read Replica', the first card founded on a verb that required the session-6 roster extension, 'Verb: isolate and throttle. The boss is a split brain.' (:2249 verbatim) (12 of the 20-type launch canon, OD-14(a)). Slice shape mirrors the eleven shipped g1 siblings: a reconnaissance opening on the calmest loud floor in the game, a peak built from the line's two native crowds (held connections and app-team tickets), a trough where the enemy is a copy that stopped answering and a neighbour eating the drum, a surprise-with-composition wave carrying the line's signature event — the unindexed scan, Debuffer's home level — landing beside the upgrade nobody asked for, and a finale built on the card's own catastrophe: the stampede that melts a DB 'sized for a cached world' and the seam that opens between two ledgers while every gauge stays lit. Deliberately RULES-FREE (no rules block): §2.24 rule-carrier values stay in the g1 slices until the batch-D rule-adapter pass reads them for cross-type tables.

waves.title: key.wave.1
waves.note: Rule (b) honoured: first wave of any level ALWAYS <=40% of par (§1.7). Cold Start Minute governs the first 90s of sim-time: handover no threat, one FREE conversion, signature constraint asserts harmlessly with telegraph (§1.9). On this line the harmless assertion is the workday chatter landing clean inside a wide-open pool — slips across the counter, the lag ribbon slack, the heartbeat pulse steady at transaction rate, and the only anomalies are the small grey questions the cellar learns to ask out loud: a scanner's drizzle at the edge asking which databases are shy, a query plan that reads like a shrug, a tenant asking whether the replica is 'real-time real-time'. The quarter opens bright because §8.10 says this floor hides nothing — 'heavy, central, well-lit objects with visible replication streams' (verbatim) — and the card says what that light is for: 'You run the thing that cannot lose data, for people who will write terrible queries against it' (§1.3 verbatim).

waves.title: key.wave.2
waves.note: Rising floor beat one — the ROUTINE catastrophe, and it is the line's two native crowds arriving together. Two-Front (§2.24): the pool fills with holders (Sapper — 'one slow connection held open is a slot that never frees'; the registry's sipper re-worn from web sockets to the connection pool of §3.3's patience column, 'Connection pool exhausted' verbatim, which §4.3 calls 'the number-one real cause of "the site is down"') spending concurrency on slowness that is individually unremarkable, while the app teams' desk begins its climb (Swarm — the hydra of write-then-read confusion, 'I placed my order and it's gone', §4.3 verbatim) spending hands on tickets whose only honest answer is a routing upgrade the player hasn't bought yet. Two tenants of the same moment, two instruments, one lesson of wave two: the present is what you cannot lose, and readable is not the same as true (§1.x :908 'degraded is harder to read than dead', verbatim core).
waves.entropyNote: entropy budget here = f(estate age x size x (1 - maintenance spend)), NOT wave number (§2.24) — on this line maintenance spend IS the indexer and the monitor: 'query monitoring' and 'per-tenant throttling and isolation' are the registry's own counter list for this level's signature threat (§2.5), and the card prices the unspent version in its first sentence: 'people who will write terrible queries against it'.

waves.title: key.wave.3
waves.note: Rule (c): 30% is 50% below the preceding peak (60%) — >=45% satisfied. Dips are where the player builds (§1.7): the quorum witness, the fencing switch, the read-your-writes routing and the card-catalogue indexer all get their window here. But on this line the quiet has an attention problem: the neighbour's batch job has settled into the drum like a elbow in the ribs ('60% of the box's I/O degrading 200 neighbours invisibly until churn', registry §2.10 verbatim — the Parasite wearing IOPS instead of inodes), and the flapping fleet behind the mesh is a trust account withdrawing in silence — 'failovers triggered by a network blip' (§4.3 verbatim) leave a ribbon that reads calm because the replica acks lie prettily. Two fronts: concurrency x reputation — held IOPS starve the workday chatter while the spiral makes the half-dead replicas themselves the story the postmortem starts telling.
waves.note2: the trough is also the silent-stop's middle frame: nothing visible happens for exactly the reason §4.3 gives — 'a replica that silently stops replicating while still answering queries' — the ribbon is flat because the ribbon is the lie's witness.

waves.title: key.wave.4
waves.note: Compound-wave exemplar, cellar variant: the scan and the window land together — 'One tenant's unindexed analytical query starves everyone else's transactions; a backup takes a lock that blocks writes' (§2.11 :9849 verbatim; Debuffer debuts here, the every-4th-wave NEW ROLE beat, unseen in waves 1-3 — and this is the Debuffer's HOME level, the registry's one throttle-everyone mechanic wearing the §3.1 band verbatim: 400-4,000ms 'the Noisy Query's actual weapon'), while the major-version gate the player scheduled (or didn't) opens at 'a time chosen by someone else' (Splitter debuts too — mod-update-day re-framed onto §1.3's 'maintenance window your customers will not accept', the upgrade the doc promised wearing the dependency's calendar). Two fronts: concurrency (the pool dies one held slot at a time) x data-integrity (the lock that blocks writes is a correctness question asked by a calendar). secondIncident inside the same window because on this line every failure is two failures: the query that grew and the schema that never was.
waves.secondIncident: the upgrade window finds the scan mid-flight -> 1.8x multiplier applies (stated openly in the Codex, §2.24).

waves.title: key.wave.5
waves.note: The finale is the tier lesson completed: 'HA introduces its own failure class — split-brain, failover storms and stampedes exist *because* you added redundancy' (§1.x :908 verbatim), and the class arrives as one bad second multiplied — the cache reboots into a 100% miss wall and 'every visitor hits the DB at once' (signature moment verbatim; Tank — the registry's one raw-volume entry re-worn INBOUND: this flood is not amplification, it is coalescing failing, the uncoalesced million arriving at a drum sized for a cached world, §4.3 'instantly melts' verbatim core), while the straight-faced reads hold the floor calm for exactly the seconds the writes need to fork (Mimic — 'serving stale data with a straight face', §4.3 verbatim core; the reads smiling as the seam opens — 'two ledgers diverging with an angry red seam between them', §1.3 catastrophe verbatim; the boss with no registry id arrives as the envelope event, bundle threats._todo carries the proposal). Hard wave draws TWO fronts — bandwidth x concurrency — per §2.24: the pipe into the drum and the slots inside it. Win check: the quorum held, the ribbon stayed honest, no second primary ever took a write, and the seam stayed a picture in the Codex instead of a state on the board.
waves.triageWindow: after any catastrophic failure in this wave: arrivals queue visibly outside, patience draining, hands freed 30s (§1.7).
